newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends slghtly up on dollar supply.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends slghtly up on dollar supply.

text.p: The won closed slightly higher against the dollar on Tuesday as dollar supply offset early losses of the local unit on short-cover dollar buying, dealers said.
The won closed at the day's high of 820.20, against the opening rate of 820.50. It touched a low of 821.50.

"Recent strength of the local currency boosted dollar buying by banks to cover their short dollar positions," said a dealer at Chase Manhattan Bank. Dealers said the won had gained strength on the back of an anticipated dollar supply after the increase in the foreign shareholding limit.

The foreign shareholding ceiling is due to be raised to 20 percent of a local listed stock on October 1 from the current 18 percent. Dealers predict the increased ceiling would bring in as much as $1 billion in foreign fund into the local bourse.
"The dollar will stay weak tomorrow. The ceiling rise, Chusok and export deals will be among major factors to depress the dollar tomorrow," said a Korea Exchange Bank dealer.
Dealers saw the won's range at between 820.00 and 822.00 on Wednesday and the base mid-rate at around 820.60. Tuesday's mid-rate was pegged at 821.20.
